input.summary: Bunkhouse log shell: parts/bunkhouse.mjs unchanged. The part places 510 blocks, all on palette, 0 refused; its alone-run report shows only the roof's off-palette.
left: OFF-PALETTE polished_deepslate_stairs x22 and polished_deepslate_slab x8 come from roof.json (cottage, slate), not from parts/bunkhouse.mjs. runParts lays the roof right after the first part and attributes it to the shell. Fixing it means editing roof.json (Roofs part) or palette.json: use palette-listed slate stairs and slabs (cobbled_deepslate_stairs/slab or deepslate_tile_stairs/slab), or add polished_deepslate_stairs and polished_deepslate_slab to palette roofs. Not done: both are outside bunkhouse.mjs and I was told to edit only that file.

make.sh fails before it writes anything: parts/roofs.mjs line 7 reads ../roof-sawmill.json at import time and that file does not exist yet. This is the Roofs part's problem. build.nbt is stale (08:46), and parts-report.json is also from the last successful run.
REFUSED: none for this part. It is the first part, so nothing earlier can block its writes. Refused 0 in parts-report.json and in my scratch run.

waste.what: make.sh could not show this part's report line because another part's import error (roofs.mjs reading a missing roof-sawmill.json) aborted the whole build. I wrote a scratch harness in /tmp to run the bunkhouse part alone with roof.json and read its report.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one 20-line scratch script
waste.tool: `node build.mjs --only "Bunkhouse log shell"` (run one part plus the roof), or runParts catching a throwing part and still writing parts-report.json with the error on that line

waste.what: I checked by hand whether the off-palette blocks were mine: searched palette.json for polished_deepslate_stairs (absent), then read roof.json and the layRoof source to confirm the roof produced them.
waste.tool: `mcd roof --spec roof.json --palette palette.json` should swap the slate preset's stairs and slabs for palette-listed ids and print each swap; a roof that reports its own OFF-PALETTE blocks would have named the file and the fix

waste.what: runParts attributes the roof's off-palette blocks to the first part (the shell), so this part's line blames it for blocks it never wrote.
waste.cost: one misdirected fix attempt, avoided by reading the source
waste.tool: runParts should list roof off-palette under its own line ("Roofs (roof.json)") instead of the shell's

companions.task: choose the slate stair and slab ids that exist in palette.json (cobbled_deepslate or deepslate_tile courses) for the cottage roof, or confirm the palette should gain the polished_deepslate stair and slab; check the tones match the slate roof.
